paras: The assault on an elderly Black man on the Cairo levee was a beating of an unnamed "old negro man" by a gang on the Ohio levee at Cairo, Illinois, on Christmas Day 1881. One of the attackers, a white man named Wm. Carroll, was arrested about two weeks later and fined five dollars and costs.

According to the Cairo Bulletin, Carroll was "one of a gang who attacked and brutally beat an old negro man on Ohio levee on Christmas day." The report did not name the victim or the other members of the gang, and it gave no cause for the attack and no account of the old man's injuries.

Carroll had been away from Cairo after the assault and returned only on the Sunday before his arrest. Constable Haz. Martin arrested him on January 9, 1882, the day before the report appeared. In Magistrate Comings' court he was fined five dollars and costs, the same penalty the court gave that day to a Black man arrested for being drunk and disorderly. No report of arrests of the other attackers appears in the coverage.

The only account found is a short item in the "Police Notes" column of the Daily Cairo Bulletin on January 10, 1882. The column ran the case alongside a drunkenness arrest and the capture of a card sharper from Golconda, treating it as routine court business. The Bulletin identified both Carroll and the victim by race and said the gang had "brutally beat" the old man, but offered no further comment. No first report of the Christmas Day assault and no coverage in other papers were found.
